$comment: The combat sounds (sea battles): rendered by combat-sfx.py from CC0 / public-domain recordings (cut points there), not by prepare.ts, which merges these credits and groups into art/audio/CREDITS.json and sfx/sfx.json as they are.

credits.title: 01 Salute Cannon Reveille (The Hellcats: A Day in the Life)
credits.author: United States Military Academy Band, The Hellcats (individual performer not named; Commons lists the author as unknown)
credits.notes: The salute cannon that opens the track: 0.40-2.85s, cut before the bugle reveille starts ~3s in. Real field-piece shot with a natural outdoor tail. Commons template {{PD-USGov}}. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: GunShotGverb (Tiny Naval Battle Sounds Set)
credits.author: qubodup (Iwan Gabovitch)
credits.notes: Whole 2s file. Made from US military video audio and pdsounds.tuxfamily.org public-domain recordings (pack README); a modern naval gun with artificial (GVerb) reverb added by the author. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: cannon_02 (25 CC0 bang / firework SFX)
credits.author: rubberduck
credits.notes: A recorded firework mortar "cannon" bang, whole file; lighter than a real gun, so play pitched down (0.6-0.8). Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Fireworks in distance - 1
credits.author: ezwa
credits.notes: One distant bang with echo, 4.9-6.6s of the 67s recording (New Year fireworks across the Belgian countryside); faint crackle under the tail. Commons licence template {{PD-author}} (released into the public domain by the author, worldwide) via PDSounds.org. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Fireworks in distance - 1
credits.author: ezwa
credits.notes: A longer rolling distant boom, 8.2-10.5s of the recording. Commons licence template {{PD-author}} (released into the public domain by the author, worldwide) via PDSounds.org. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Fireworks in distance - 5
credits.author: ezwa
credits.notes: A single sharper distant report, 19.5-20.7s of the 50s recording. Commons licence template {{PD-author}} (released into the public domain by the author, worldwide) via PDSounds.org. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Cannonball passing overhead (synthesised, variant a)
credits.author: Project Corsair
credits.notes: Noise through a resonant band-pass falling in pitch as the ball passes (Doppler), loudest just after it goes over; made with ball-whistle.py and judged with earshot (reads as a whoosh past, where the slowed stick swishes it replaces read as a stick).

credits.title: Cannonball passing overhead (synthesised, variant c)
credits.author: Project Corsair
credits.notes: Noise through a resonant band-pass falling in pitch as the ball passes (Doppler), loudest just after it goes over; made with ball-whistle.py and judged with earshot (reads as a whoosh past, where the slowed stick swishes it replaces read as a stick).

credits.title: Cannonball passing overhead (synthesised, variant b)
credits.author: Project Corsair
credits.notes: Noise through a resonant band-pass falling in pitch as the ball passes (Doppler), loudest just after it goes over; made with ball-whistle.py and judged with earshot (reads as a whoosh past, where the slowed stick swishes it replaces read as a stick).

credits.title: wood_breaking_01 (100 CC0 metal and wood SFX)
credits.author: rubberduck
credits.notes: Short wood break/crunch, whole file. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: wood_breaking_02 (100 CC0 metal and wood SFX)
credits.author: rubberduck
credits.notes: Short wood break/crunch, whole file. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Velcro_01 (202 More Sound Effects)
credits.author: OwlishMedia
credits.notes: A velcro rip standing in for canvas tearing; no CC0/PD fabric-rip recording was found. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Velcro_02 (202 More Sound Effects)
credits.author: OwlishMedia
credits.notes: A shorter velcro rip, canvas-tear stand-in. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: paper_ripped - 1 (Various paper sound effects)
credits.author: Luckius
credits.notes: A quick paper rip, canvas-tear stand-in; layer under a velcro rip or play pitched down. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: tree chop fall thud
credits.author: kheetor
credits.notes: 0.95s to the end of the 2.67s file: past the axe chops, into the creak, crack and fall thud. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: wood_cracking_04, _02, _03 and wood_falling_05 (100 CC0 metal and wood SFX)
credits.author: rubberduck
credits.notes: Three short wood cracks then a wood fall from the same pack, placed in sequence (0, 0.30, 0.62, 1.05s) to make one split-and-fall. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Black Powder
credits.author: kurt
credits.notes: One black-powder gun shot, 0.05-0.75s of the 4s file (six shots). Recorded with some echo, per the uploader. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Black Powder
credits.author: kurt
credits.notes: Another black-powder shot, 1.50-2.20s of the same file. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: sword_clash 1, 3, 5, 8, 2, 6 (20 Sword Sound Effects - Attacks and Clashes)
credits.author: StarNinjas
credits.notes: Six blade clashes from the pack (two knives struck together) placed at 0, 0.85, 1.4, 2.55, 3.2 and 4.3s to make a 5.5s exchange; layer over melee_1/2. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Clapping hurray
credits.author: starlite
credits.notes: The rest of the same recording, 6.0-11.6s, fading out at its natural end. Commons licence template {{PD-author}} (released into the public domain by the author, worldwide) via PDSounds.org. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Hurray
credits.author: starlite
credits.notes: A short "hurray" shout, from 0.3s to the end. Commons licence template {{PD-author}} (released into the public domain by the author, worldwide) via PDSounds.org. Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: ExplosionMetal (Tiny Naval Battle Sounds Set)
credits.author: qubodup (Iwan Gabovitch)
credits.notes: Whole 1.5s file; version 2 of the pack, rebuilt from the author's own freesound recording 67474 (README). Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

credits.title: Explosion-LS100155
credits.author: Fg2
credits.notes: Single sharp blast, 0.80s to the end of the 1.6s file. Recorded by the uploader at the Toshogu Spring Festival, Nikko. Commons licence template {{PD-self}} (released into the public domain by the author). Mono 22.05 kHz, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS.

groups.cannon_close: A single close gun: a real salute field piece, a naval gun with reverb, a firework mortar bang; play pitched 0.85-1.1 (cannon_close_3 at 0.6-0.8) for variety.
groups.cannon_far: Distant booms (fireworks heard across open country); play low, low-passed and pitched 0.6-0.9 for an enemy broadside over the water.
groups.ball_whistle: A cannonball going over: synthesised (ball-whistle.py), a falling howl of air; play at rate 0.9-1.1.
groups.wood_hit: Short wood breaks for a ball striking the hull; play pitched 0.55-0.8 for a heavy hull, layered with a cannon_far thump.
groups.sail_tear: Stand-in rips (velcro, paper) for canvas tearing; play pitched 0.7-0.9 and layer two for a big sail.
groups.mast_crack: Timber cracking and falling for a mast going over; play pitched 0.6-0.8 for weight.
groups.musket: Black-powder shots and a ragged rifle volley for swivels and boarders; play pitched 0.9-1.1 and stagger singles for a volley.
groups.melee: Blades clashing in a boarding fight (sword clashes laid in a sequence); a musket volley plays with it. (Two crowd beds were dropped: earshot heard them as a crowd cheering.)
groups.cheer: Crew cheering on victory: clapping and "woo" from a small group, plus one "hurray"; play pitched 0.85-0.95 for rougher, deeper voices.
groups.explosion: Big blasts for a powder magazine: a single explosion, a sharp blast and a rolling chain; play pitched 0.5-0.7 for size.
